parsed.explanation: Combined regime is state-targeting, not mere disapproval: Section 377 (2-10 years) remains in active use and intensified after the 2021 coup, Police Act 35(c) allows up to three months' detention for 'suspicious' behaviour after sunset and is documented as used specifically against trans people, and militarised policing, arbitrary detention, torture and sexual violence in detention are documented. Police harassment, extortion, sexual assault, stripping/parading and beating are patterned, with no enforceable anti-discrimination protection or effective recourse. Poll support for legality and nat kadaw visibility are social signals but do not offset documented state perpetration. Killing counts lack denominators, so magnitude above background is unresolved, but severity plus frequency of custody abuse drives the score.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign documents and any discrepancy can trigger detention under Section 377 and Police Act 35(c); no traveller-facing acceptance documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Document/appearance mismatch can become investigation and detention, with no documented remedy.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police Act detention up to three months, Section 377 imprisonment, documented torture, sexual violence, rape, extortion and forced stripping in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No enforceable protection or documented effective remedy for trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for presence/decency can lead to prolonged detention and custody abuse; complaint risks further enforcement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No legal gender recognition or recognised identity; vague public-decency and obscenity provisions used against LGBTQ people; birth-sex placement is the operative default implied by non-recognition, exact ward rule not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Non-recognition interacts with police and custody encounters, increasing outing and misplacement risk.

care_services.exposure: 2022 Gender Policy is non-binding planning document; no enforceable care protection documented; detention-related medication denial not specifically documented.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care after police/custody exposure would occur within the same hostile, non-recognising system.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Section 377, Police Act 35(c), public-decency/morality provisions, book bans and militarised policing frame trans/LGBT people as targets; enforcement intensified post-coup.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Broadcasting guidelines and child-rights clause are non-enforceable and do not protect adult visitors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Multiple overlapping laws give police discretionary detention and extortion levers at any encounter.

minors_guardians.exposure: Child Rights non-discrimination clause lacks enforcement; no traveller-specific minor protection documented, and guardian would face the same police/detention exposure when outed.
minors_guardians.interaction: travelling adult with a minor compounds exposure because detention or outing affects the child and guardian cannot invoke a protective regime.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented police harassment, sexual assault including rape, mistreatment, extortion, and 5-12 plus 17 raw killing counts in state/province areas; per-capita magnitude unresolved.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented prosecution of attackers or police discipline; survey fear/no-confidence is undated and not relied on for rate.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are documented perpetrators rather than protectors, so street violence and state abuse converge.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No enforceable anti-discrimination law; NGO registration law carries prison terms, constraining advocates; remedies repeatedly absent.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of recourse magnifies every other exposure; unknowns on entry, wards and frequency do not resolve toward safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: repeated police targeting, imprisonment and sexual violence in custody with courts/police as threat. This case has less documented presentation-only convictions, hence slightly above 0.15, but torture and militarised detention keep it in the severe band.

Lower (less safe) than 0.25-A: that anchor has short detention and sexual harassment without documented post-coup torture, intensified Section 377 enforcement and multi-law police detention up to three months.

Materially lower than 0.35-C: police extortion there usually ends in release after payment; here documented rape, torture, prolonged detention and imprisonment exposure make outing consequences far more severe.

parsed.synthesis: If outed, the traveller faces the state as perpetrator: discretionary night detention, Section 377 prosecution, extortion, sexual violence and torture, with no operative remedy. Social poll support and a visible spirit-medium role show trans people are not socially invisible, but they do not restrain police, courts or militarised enforcement, and non-recognition leaves documents and placement to official discretion. Compared with anchors, this is a severe-risk combined regime: organised state targeting with major custody harms, below high-risk examples where detention is shorter and torture is not documented.
